problem_motivation.content: The current AI materials-discovery paradigm is limited by a synthesisability gap despite producing many candidate structures.
problem_motivation.evidence_span:
The current structure-centric paradigm in artificial intelligence-
driven materials discovery, despite delivering thousands of
candidate structures, is stalling at a critical barrier: the
synthesisability gap.

problem_motivation.content: Structure-centric generative and screening approaches fail at experimental realization, creating a synthesisability gap.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: The field now confronts a decisive bottleneck: structure-centric approaches-whether traditional DFT screening or modern artificial intelligence (AI) generative models often trained on DFT data-routinely falter when their predictions meet experimental synthesis, exposing a critical synthesisability gap.

problem_motivation.content: The synthesisability gap is framed as a fundamental limitation of structure-centric approaches.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Having established the synthesisability gap as a fundamental limitation of structure-centric approaches

problem_motivation.content: The practical utility of structure-centric generative models is limited by the synthesisability gap.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: the practical utility of structure-centric generative models is limited by the synthesisability gap

problem_motivation.content: The synthesisability gap exposes a fundamental limitation of the structure-property paradigm in de novo design.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Ultimately, the synthesisability gap reveals a fundamental limitation of the structure-property paradigm in de novo design

problem_motivation.content: A synthesis-first paradigm requires new AI/ML tools for representing, predicting from, and inverting synthesis protocols.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Realising the vision of a synthesis-first paradigm requires a new class of AI/ML tools.

problem_motivation.content: Three core technical challenges are protocol representation, property prediction, and inverse design of new protocols.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Three key technical challenges emerge: (i) how to represent a synthesis protocol, (ii) how to predict properties from that representation, and (iii) how to invert the model to design new protocols.

problem_motivation.content: Data scarcity, low quality, and limited accessibility are the most immediate barrier to adoption.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Data scarcity, quality and accessibility. This represents the most immediate barrier to widespread adoption.

problem_motivation.content: A primary challenge is robust transfer from narrow SDL regimes to broad literature chemistry.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Primary challenge: Achieving robust transfer across domains- from narrow SDL regimes to literature-scale chemistry-requires principled domain adaptation and transfer learning, with careful handling of covariate and label shifts.

problem_motivation.content: Diverse protocol formats hinder interoperability.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: The diversity of text snippets, SMILES strings, reaction graphs and action sequences hampers model interoperability.

problem_motivation.content: Deep models trained on narrow domains often fail to generalize to unseen reactions.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Deep models trained on narrow chemical domains often fail on unseen reactions.

problem_motivation.content: Real robotic SDL platforms still have substantial failure rates, require oversight, and lack user-friendly interfaces.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: yet real-world robotic platforms still incur nontrivial failure rates (10%–30%), require human-in-the-loop oversight, and often lack chemist-friendly interfaces.

problem_motivation.content: There is an executability gap between abstract protocols and reliable robotic execution under hardware variability.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Beyond algorithmic integration, there is an executability gap: mapping abstract protocols to reliable robotic execution under hardware variability (dispense precision, dead volumes, thermal lags, calibration drift).

problem_motivation.content: Benchmark coverage for inorganic synthesis and protocol-aware inverse design is still sparse.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: coverage across inorganic synthesis and protocol-aware inverse design remains sparse.

problem_motivation.content: Structure-centric approaches fail when predictions meet experimental reality, reflecting a synthesisability gap.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: The prevailing structure-property paradigm has delivered profound scientific insights and enabled remarkable computational advances, but it falters when predictions confront experimental reality.

problem_motivation.content: The synthesisability gap is a fundamental limitation of structure-centric methods.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: The persistent synthesisability gap-where fewer than 2% of computationally predicted phases are ever realised-represents not merely a technical hurdle but a fundamental architectural limitation of structure-centric approaches.

prior_approach.content: High-throughput DFT workflows and major materials databases have been used to discover low-enthalpy candidates.
prior_approach.evidence_span: High-throughput density functional theory (DFT) workflows and large databases such as the Materials Project, AFLOW and the open quantum materials database (OQMD) have delivered thousands of low-enthalpy candidates

prior_approach.content: Related prior ideas include autonomous experimentation, retrosynthesis planning, and closed-loop reaction optimization.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Related ideas already exist in autonomous experimentation, retrosynthesis planning and closed-loop reaction optimisation [6–9].

prior_approach.content: Organic retrosynthesis heuristics and planners such as synthetic accessibility metrics, ASKCOS, and AiZynthFinder are established prior tools.
prior_approach.evidence_span: While organic retrosynthesis heuristics (e.g. synthetic accessibility, synthetic complexity, and retrosynthetic accessibility scores) and planners (e.g. ASKCOS and AiZynthFinder [7, 10]) are mature for molecular synthesis

prior_approach.content: Generative AI models such as VAEs, GANs, diffusion, autoregressive, and flow models have been used to propose new materials structures.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Generative AI models have emerged as powerful tools for exploring chemical space and proposing novel material structures de novo

prior_approach.content: Post-hoc heuristic filters like SAScore, SCScore, and RAScore are used to compensate for synthesisability issues.
prior_approach.evidence_span: post-hoc heuristics such as the synthetic accessibility score (SAScore) [18], synthetic complexity score (SCScore) [22], and retrosynthetic accessibility score (RAScore) [23] are often applied to filter generative outputs.

prior_approach.content: A complementary prior approach is supervised learning to predict synthesisability directly for hypothetical crystalline materials.
prior_approach.evidence_span: A complementary strategy is to predict synthesisability directly with supervised learning, treating it as a classification or ranking problem rather than as a downstream constraint applied post hoc.

prior_approach.content: Physics-informed neural networks and hybrid surrogate models embed differential-equation constraints for synthesis modeling.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and other hybrid surrogate models that embed differential-equation constraints offer a promising but challenging avenue for synthesis modelling

prior_approach.content: Physics-based simulators such as kinetic Monte Carlo, phase-field, CALPHAD-informed diffusion, and CFD provide mechanistic priors.
prior_approach.evidence_span: physics-based synthesis models-including kinetic Monte Carlo for surface reactions and nucleation, phase-field models for crystallisation, coarsening and porosity evolution, CALculation of PHAse diagrams (CALPHAD)-informed diffusion models for multi-component solids, and computational fluid dynamics for reactor-scale transport-provide mechanistic constraints and synthetic inductive bias

prior_approach.content: Structural resources and DFT workflows can contribute constraints, descriptors, route screening, and priors to protocol-centric design.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Vast structural resources (e.g. Materials Project [2], OQMD [4]) and DFT workflows must be central to protocol-centric design, not peripheral. They contribute: (i) Phase-diagram and thermochemical constraints

prior_approach.content: Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, generative models, and invertible inverse models are emerging approaches for protocol inverse design.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
Several complementary algorithmic families have emerged for this task:
•  BO
•  RL
•  Generative models
•  Invertible and probabilistic inverse models

prior_approach.content: Rule-based symbolic retrosynthesis planners like ASKCOS and AiZynthFinder can be combined with BO or RL for hybrid planning.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Rule-based symbolic retrosynthesis planners such as ASKCOS and AiZynthFinder provide chemistry-aware search primitives that can be combined with BO or RL for hybrid planning

prior_approach.content: Examples include VAEs for multistep polymer syntheses, SynFormer for reaction sequences, MINERVA SDL, and autonomous flow quantum-dot synthesis.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Gómez-Bombarelli et al [12] used VAEs to generate multi-step polymer syntheses (organic analogue), while Tadanki et al [47] introduced SynFormer, a Transformer that outputs full reaction sequences. More directly relevant to inorganic materials, SDL platforms such as MINERVA seamlessly link protocol generation with robotic execution [9], and autonomous flow platforms have demonstrated multistep quantum-dot synthesis

prior_approach.content: Event-sourced and streaming architectures such as ESAMP and MDML have been proposed for provenance and experiment control.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Event-sourced and streaming architectures adapted from distributed systems have been proposed for materials provenance and experiment control (e.g. ESAMP and MDML)

prior_limitation.content: Many theoretically promising candidates from structure-centric pipelines remain unrealized experimentally.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: yet many theoretically promising structures remain unrealised in the laboratory

prior_limitation.content: Existing ingredients are not sufficiently unified for inorganic materials discovery under a protocol-first formalism.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Our claim is not that these ingredients are themselves new, but that in inorganic materials discovery they remain insufficiently unified by a protocol-first formalism

prior_limitation.content: Organic retrosynthesis tools are only partially applicable to solid-state and solvothermal materials.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: they are only partially applicable to solid-state and solvothermal materials.

prior_limitation.content: Even advanced structure-centric surrogate models remain fundamentally limited by their structure-centric basis.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Even advanced surrogate models-such as energy-conserving equivariant graph neural networks [21] that provide symmetry-respecting predictions with near-DFT accuracy-remain fundamentally limited by their structure-centric foundation.

prior_limitation.content: These heuristics correlate only weakly with true experimental difficulty.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: These heuristics, however, are only loosely correlated with true experimental difficulty

prior_limitation.content: Explicit retrosynthesis at the scale of millions of generated candidates remains computationally prohibitive.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: explicit retrosynthesis for millions of candidates remains prohibitive at library-generation scale.

prior_limitation.content: Direct synthesisability predictors inherit reporting and attempt biases, and the synthesisable label is context dependent.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Such predictors are promising but must be interpreted carefully: they inherit biases in what the community has attempted and reported, and the target label (‘synthesisable’) is itself time-, platform- and effort-dependent.

prior_limitation.content: Protocol-centric implementation differs from organic synthesis because inorganic synthesis is affected by phase equilibria, non-equilibrium processing, and transport-limited kinetics.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: not assuming their direct transfer to inorganic synthesis governed by phase equilibria, non-equilibrium processing and transport-limited kinetics.

prior_limitation.content: No single protocol representation is universally best for inorganic synthesis.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: no single representation is universally best for inorganic synthesis.

prior_limitation.content: Model accuracy is limited more by scarce and poor-quality paired protocol-property data than by algorithm choice.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Model accuracy is limited less by algorithmic nuance than by the scarcity and quality of paired protocol-property datasets

prior_limitation.content: Practical end-to-end deployments of PINNs for full multi-step protocols are still difficult and rare.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: robust practical deployments for full, multi-step protocols remain difficult and comparatively scarce, with most demonstrations focusing on constrained unit operations rather than end-to-end recipes.

prior_limitation.content: These physics-based tools are computationally intensive, hard to parameterize for new chemistries, and limited for unknown multicomponent systems.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Today, these tools are computationally intensive, difficult to parameterise for novel chemistries, and often limited in predictive power for unknown, multi-component systems.

prior_limitation.content: Hybrid integration of structural knowledge is not plug-and-play because structural characterization is sparse, noisy, and multimodal.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: In practice, however, hybrid integration is rarely plug-and-play: structural characterisation is often sparse, noisy, and multi-modal

prior_limitation.content: Existing literature data are unstructured, biased, incomplete, and often proprietary.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Existing literature is dominated by unstructured prose, publication bias toward positive results, missing metadata, and proprietary restrictions.

prior_limitation.content: Text-mined literature data are heterogeneous and biased, while SDL datasets are narrow and domain-specific.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: data pulled from text-mined literature are heterogeneous and biased toward successful experiments, whereas self-driving laboratories yield highly structured but domain-specific datasets.

prior_limitation.content: These provenance architectures are complex and not widely adopted.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: but remain complex to implement and have not yet seen widespread community adoption.

prior_limitation.content: Automating inorganic workflows is harder than liquid handling, especially for solids and furnace operations.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: For inorganic workflows, solids handling (grinding/milling, weighing powders), pellet pressing, high-temperature furnace loading/unloading, atmosphere control and thermal profile verification remain difficult to automate robustly compared to liquid handling.

prior_limitation.content: Current atomistic and continuum simulations rarely provide end-to-end predictive control for complex inorganic synthesis.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, present-day atomistic and continuum tools rarely provide end-to-end predictive control over synthesis outcomes for complex inorganic systems.

rejected_alternative.content: Rather than treating only atomic configurations as primary variables, the paper advocates treating executable synthesis protocols as primary design variables.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span:
We argue that closing this gap demands a pivot
to a synthesis-first paradigm in which executable synthesis

protocols, not just atomic configurations, are treated as primary
design variables.

rejected_alternative.content: The paper does not assume direct transfer of organic synthesis tools to inorganic synthesis because inorganic synthesis is governed by different phenomena.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: using organic tools (e.g. the simplified molecular input line entry system (SMILES), SELF-referencIng embedded strings (SELFIES), and retrosynthesis planners) as analogies where instructive but not assuming their direct transfer to inorganic synthesis governed by phase equilibria, non-equilibrium processing and transport-limited kinetics.

rejected_alternative.content: The perspective rejects treating autonomous labs only as execution layers or retrosynthesis only as route generators, instead coupling representation, modeling, design, characterization, and execution.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: This framing differs from treating autonomous laboratories merely as execution layers or treating retrosynthesis tools merely as route generators: here, representation, forward modelling, inverse design, characterisation and execution are posed as one coupled protocol-design problem.

rejected_alternative.content: Organic tools are not adopted as direct solutions; they are treated only as instructive analogues for inorganic synthesis.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: In this section we focus on inorganic-relevant approaches and treat organic tools as instructive analogues rather than direct solutions.

rejected_alternative.content: Fully lights-out autonomous operation is not the envisioned medium-term mode; human-AI collaboration is preferred because current robotic platforms are failure-prone and need oversight.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: In the medium term we therefore envision human–AI collaboration as the dominant operating mode: AI assists chemists with planning, monitoring, and failure recovery rather than operating fully lights-out.

rejected_alternative.content: A single monolithic model trained on all protocols is rejected in favor of interoperable foundation models.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: In our view, the most realistic route is not a single monolithic model trained on ‘all protocols’, but interoperable foundation models grounded in execution logs, characterisation streams and explicit ontologies

rejected_alternative.content: Relying on structure-first simulation alone is not the near-term path; protocol-centered modeling is chosen as a pragmatic alternative because current simulations lack end-to-end predictive control.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Protocol-centred modelling therefore offers a pragmatic route to progress in the near and medium term, while leaving open the long-term possibility of deeper first-principles synthesis simulation.

inspiration_source.content: Organic synthesis tools are used as analogies to inform the new framework.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: using organic tools (e.g. the simplified molecular input line entry system (SMILES), SELF-referencIng embedded strings (SELFIES), and retrosynthesis planners) as analogies where instructive

inspiration_source.content: Protocol-centric discovery should adopt lessons from adjacent ML settings about the value of failed experiments.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: The value of failed experiments for materials ML has already been demonstrated in adjacent settings, and protocol-centric discovery will benefit from adopting the same lesson early [57].

causal_claim.content: Post-hoc synthesisability filters provide only weak correlation with experimental difficulty, so they do not solve the problem.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Post-hoc synthesisability filters provide only weak correlation with experimental difficulty

causal_claim.content: The systematic failure of major generative architectures indicates that a paradigm shift to protocol-first design is needed.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This systematic failure across all major generative architectures-from VAEs to diffusion models-indicates that the solution lies not in incremental improvements to structure-centric methods, but in a fundamental paradigm shift that treats synthesis protocols as primary design objects.

causal_claim.content: Treating protocols as primary design variables directly addresses the synthesisability gap.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This approach directly addresses the synthesisability gap by treating the recipe-not just the product-as the primary design variable.

causal_claim.content: Confining search to executable procedures improves practical relevance and enables more efficient optimization over real operations.
causal_claim.evidence_span: it confines search to experimentally actionable procedures, improving relevance and enabling efficient optimisation over real operations

causal_claim.content: Explicit protocol variables allow learning of properties sensitive to process conditions like temperature ramps, solvent, pH, and aging time.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Properties that depend sensitively on temperature ramps, solvent, pH or ageing time can be learned because these variables are explicit inputs

causal_claim.content: Protocol representations naturally map to robot instructions, enabling closed-loop self-driving laboratories.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Protocol representations map naturally to robot instructions, enabling closed-loop, SDLs

causal_claim.content: Correlating process variables with performance reveals non-equilibrium effects, defect formation, and morphology control that structure-only models miss.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Correlating process variables with performance uncovers non-equilibrium effects, defect formation and morphology control invisible to equilibrium structure-only models

causal_claim.content: Including green metrics and costs directly in optimization can steer design toward deployable solutions.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Green-chemistry metrics (E-factor, process mass intensity (PMI), energy footprint) and economic costs (precursor cost, throughput, labour, equipment amortisation) can be included directly in multi-objective optimisation, steering design toward practically deployable solutions

causal_claim.content: Recent protocol-aware and SDL examples show that embedding synthesis constraints improves experimental relevance compared with structure-only approaches.
causal_claim.evidence_span: These successes, though nascent, confirm that embedding synthesis constraints can drastically improve experimental relevance compared to structure-only approaches.

causal_claim.content: Closed-loop optimization of fast-charging protocols improves Li-ion performance and mitigates degradation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Closed-loop optimisation of fast-charging protocols with ML improves performance and mitigates degradation in Li-ion cells

causal_claim.content: Combining BO with mechanistic surrogate models in flow settings reduces the number of experiments and navigates multi-objective trade-offs.
causal_claim.evidence_span: combining BO with mechanistic surrogate models reduces experiments and navigates multi-objective trade-offs

causal_claim.content: Automated spin-coating with BO has been used to co-optimize perovskite precursor composition and processing conditions.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Automated spin-coating coupled to BO has been used to co-optimise precursor composition and processing conditions for perovskite solar cells

causal_claim.content: ML-assisted real-time feedback control has steered quantum-dot growth by linking growth conditions to in situ structural observations.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Machine-learning-assisted real-time feedback control has been used to steer InAs/GaAs quantum-dot growth by coupling growth conditions to in situ reflection high-energy electron diffraction videos, which act as structure-sensitive observations of the evolving surface and quantum-dot density

causal_claim.content: Active learning with high-throughput experimentation accelerates electrocatalyst discovery and optimization.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Active learning coupled to high-throughput experimentation accelerates discovery and optimisation of electrocatalysts for CO reduction and hydrogen evolution

causal_claim.content: Interpretable ML helps reveal process-structure-property relationships for catalyst optimization.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Interpretable ML (e.g. Shapley additive explanations, SHAP) elucidates process-structure-property relationships to guide catalyst optimisation

causal_claim.content: Flow and continuous processing are especially suitable for protocol-centric optimization because they permit real-time parameter adjustment.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Flow and continuous processing environments are particularly amenable to protocol-centric optimisation because they enable real-time parameter adjustment

causal_claim.content: Embedding economic and environmental factors in protocol representations naturally supports multi-objective optimization.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Multi-objective optimisation (performance, sustainability, cost) is naturally handled when economic and environmental factors are embedded in protocol representations

causal_claim.content: Closed-loop operation with inline characterization provides the rapid feedback needed for effective learning.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Closed-loop operation with inline characterisation provides the rapid feedback necessary for effective learning

causal_claim.content: Applications are most successful when processing strongly influences final properties, the regime where structure-only methods fail.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Critically, the highest-impact applications focus on problems where processing conditions strongly influence final properties-precisely where structure-only approaches fail.

causal_claim.content: The synthesis-centric paradigm provides a demonstrated pathway to bridge the synthesisability gap and accelerate materials discovery.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The synthesis-centric paradigm is not merely a theoretical alternative but a demonstrated pathway to bridging the synthesisability gap and accelerating materials discovery.

causal_claim.content: Standardized structures and scalable structure-derived labels caused structure-centric ML to dominate historically.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The community’s historical fixation on structure is not accidental: crystal structures are comparatively well standardised; structure-derived labels (energies, band gaps, elastic constants) can be generated at scale with mature simulation workflows; and many property predictors are naturally formulated as structureproperty mappings.

causal_claim.content: Protocol heterogeneity, platform dependence, and underspecification make protocol-centered AI harder and more brittle.
causal_claim.evidence_span: By contrast, protocol data are heterogeneous, platform-dependent and often underspecified, making protocol-centred AI both harder and more brittle.

causal_claim.content: Multimodal, simulator-coupled, or experiment-in-the-loop protocol models can increase training and deployment costs relative to structure-only models.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Protocol-centric models-often featuring multimodal embeddings, simulator calls, or experiment-in-the-loop optimisation-can incur higher training and deployment costs than structure-only VAEs or diffusion networks

causal_claim.content: Multi-fidelity, surrogate, and lightweight graph-based methods can reduce computational burdens.
causal_claim.evidence_span: however, multi-fidelity, surrogate-model, and lightweight graph-based strategies can mitigate these burdens.

causal_claim.content: Protocol-aware systems can lower end-to-end discovery cost by quickly avoiding uninformative or failed experiments.
causal_claim.evidence_span: protocol-aware systems can lower end-to-end discovery cost if they rapidly avoid uninformative or failed experiments.

causal_claim.content: Treating synthesis protocols as first-class design variables embeds feasibility constraints from the outset and provides a route to bridge the gap.
causal_claim.evidence_span: By elevating synthesis protocols to first-class citizens in modelling and inverse design, the synthesis-first paradigm embeds feasibility constraints from the outset, offering a direct pathway to bridge this divide.

causal_claim.content: Embedding experimental constraints greatly improves hit rates relative to structure-only approaches.
causal_claim.evidence_span: embedding experimental constraints dramatically improves hit rates compared to structure-only approaches.

causal_claim.content: Protocol representations, physics-informed models, and hybrid integration strategies together indicate a faster and more reliable path to functional materials.
causal_claim.evidence_span: These advances collectively point toward an accelerated, more reliable route to functional materials.

mechanism_principle.content: Neglecting kinetics, precursor availability, and practical constraints explains the poor experimental realization of structure-centric predictions.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: underscoring the limitations of pipelines that neglect kinetics, precursor availability and practical constraints

mechanism_principle.content: Unknown pathways, unavailable precursors, impractical conditions, kinetic traps, purification issues, scale-up, and safety constraints contribute to the synthesisability gap.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
Key contributing factors include:
•  Unknown or infeasible reaction pathways
•  Precursor availability and cost
•  Impractical reaction conditions
•  Kinetic traps and competing reactions
•  Purification and isolation challenges
•  Scalability
•  Regulatory, safety or environmental constraints

mechanism_principle.content: Structure-only optimization fails because it assumes synthesis is a downstream solvable task, whereas synthetic constraints define accessible chemical space.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Thus, structure-only optimisation implicitly assumes synthesis is a solvable downstream task, whereas in reality synthetic constraints define the accessible chemical space.

mechanism_principle.content: Higher success probability comes not from executability alone but from combining constraints with uncertainty-aware selection, structure-sensitive feedback, and iterative refinement.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In practice, higher success probability comes not from executability alone but from combining such constraints with uncertainty-aware model selection, structure-sensitive feedback, and iterative closed-loop refinement.

mechanism_principle.content: These structural differences explain why realistic roadmaps should prioritize standardization, provenance, and robust execution.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Recognising these structural reasons is important for designing realistic roadmaps that prioritise standardisation, provenance and robust execution.

mechanism_principle.content: Because protocol-aware methods affect laboratory efficiency, scientific yield per total lab-plus-compute budget is the relevant metric.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: For this reason, the relevant metric is not model floating point operations in isolation but scientific yield per unit of combined laboratory and compute budget.

mechanism_principle.content: Protocol models are harder to universalize because protocols depend on platform-specific vocabularies, incomplete provenance, temporal logic, and multimodal hardware-linked data.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: because protocols depend on platform-specific action vocabularies, incomplete provenance, temporal control logic and the coupling of textual, sensor and hardware data.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors propose that closing the synthesisability gap requires shifting to a synthesis-first paradigm where executable protocols are primary design variables.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span:
We argue that closing this gap demands a pivot
to a synthesis-first paradigm in which executable synthesis

protocols, not just atomic configurations, are treated as primary
design variables.

hypothesis_statement.content: Closing the synthesisability gap requires a synthesis-first paradigm using executable protocols as primary design variables.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We contend that closing this gap demands a synthesis-first paradigm in which executable synthesis protocols, not just atomic configurations, are treated as the primary design variables.

hypothesis_statement.content: Hybrid protocol-aware pipelines are needed because thermodynamic stability alone is insufficient for practical viability.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: thermodynamic stability alone is an insufficient metric of practical viability; hybrid pipelines that couple structure-centric tools with protocol-aware planners are needed to bridge from virtual candidates to executable recipes.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors propose elevating synthesis protocols to first-class design objects in a synthesis protocol-property framework.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We propose elevating synthesis protocols to first-class design objects in a synthesis protocol–property framework that embeds experimental feasibility from the outset.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors advocate hierarchical Bayesian or GP multi-fidelity models to combine literature and SDL data with error correction.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We advocate hierarchical Bayesian or Gaussian-process multi-fidelity modelling to fuse literature-scale low-fidelity data with high-fidelity SDL measurements, coupled to explicit measurement-error models and batch-effect correction.

hypothesis_statement.content: Adding physical priors, uncertainty quantification, and interpretable architectures should improve trust and insight.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Incorporating physical priors, providing uncertainty quantification and employing interpretable architectures (e.g. latent-space attention visualisation, SHAP) will build trust and insight [53].

hypothesis_statement.content: Human-AI collaboration will likely dominate medium-term SDL operation rather than fully autonomous labs.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In the medium term we therefore envision human–AI collaboration as the dominant operating mode: AI assists chemists with planning, monitoring, and failure recovery rather than operating fully lights-out.

hypothesis_statement.content: Protocol-space foundation models are plausible but harder to universalize than structure models.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We consider protocol-space foundation models plausible, but harder to universalise than structure models because protocols depend on platform-specific action vocabularies, incomplete provenance, temporal control logic and the coupling of textual, sensor and hardware data.

hypothesis_statement.content: The most realistic path is interoperable foundation models grounded in logs, characterization, and ontologies with uncertainty over out-of-distribution actions.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In our view, the most realistic route is not a single monolithic model trained on ‘all protocols’, but interoperable foundation models grounded in execution logs, characterisation streams and explicit ontologies that permit transfer across platforms while preserving uncertainty about out-of-distribution actions.

hypothesis_statement.content: Protocol-first and structure-first approaches are complementary.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We view protocol-first and structure-first approaches as complementary.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors envision a 2035 ecosystem where synthesis protocols become primary design variables integrated with autonomy and real-time characterization.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We envision a materials discovery ecosystem where synthesis protocols are the primary design variables, increasingly integrated with autonomous experimentation and real-time characterisation.

hypothesis_statement.content: They expect the synthesisability gap to narrow as these elements mature and interoperate.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We expect the synthesisability gap to narrow substantially as these elements mature and interoperate.

hypothesis_statement.content: Embedding experimental reality into computational frameworks can transform materials science into executable design.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: By embracing protocols as design objects and embedding experimental reality into our computational frameworks, we can transform materials science from a discipline of discovery to one of design-one executable recipe at a time.

evidence_result.content: Only a small fraction of low-enthalpy phases found in high-throughput surveys have been realized experimentally.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Fewer than 2 % of over 50 000 low-enthalpy phases identified in high-throughput surveys have been realised experimentally

evidence_result.content: Experimental chemists often cannot realize computationally designed structures in the lab.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Experimental chemists frequently struggle to realise these computationally designed structures in the laboratory.

evidence_result.content: Case studies show protocol-aware AI is moving from proof-of-concept to practical impact across materials domains.
evidence_result.evidence_span: These case studies demonstrate that protocol-aware AI is transitioning from proof-of-concept to practical impact across diverse materials domains.

evidence_result.content: Earlier sections provide evidence that the synthesis-first paradigm is necessary and achievable.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The evidence presented in sections 2–5 demonstrates that this paradigm shift is both necessary and achievable.

evidence_result.content: Early successes include protocol-optimized batteries and self-driving quantum-dot synthesis.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Early successes-from protocol-optimised battery electrolytes to self-driving quantum dot synthesis-confirm

constraint.evidence_span:
